data.reasoning: Report 2 successfully audited all three maintainer files and found standard AUR packaging: PKGBUILD fetches a pinned release tarball from the official GitHub repository with valid SHA256 checksum, uses typical Python build tools (python -m build, python -m installer), and contains no dangerous commands or suspicious network requests. The minor sed fix to setup.py version constraint is routine. Report 1's inconclusive verdict resulted from LLM API errors (HTTP 400) during file review, not from security concerns. The initial PKGBUILD parse audit in Report 1 also confirmed no malicious execution during makepkg sourcing.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement is not a genuine security disagreement but rather a tool failure. Report 1 experienced HTTP 400 errors when attempting to audit PKGBUILD and .gitignore, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. Report 2 completed its audit successfully and found no issues. Both reports agree on the .SRCINFO being safe, and Report 1's initial PKGBUILD parse audit (before the full file review) also found it safe.
coverage_issues: Report 1 failed to complete audit due to LLM API errors (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) for PKGBUILD and .gitignore files
learnings: API errors during file review should not override successful initial parse audits - consider weighting initial safety checks more heavily when full review fails
Implement retry logic or fallback mechanisms for transient API errors to avoid inconclusive verdicts when partial audit data is available
Separate the concerns of 'makepkg parse safety' (which succeeded in Report 1) from 'full file content review' to provide more granular verdicts when one fails
